issue: Does the no-proximate-cause rule that applies to drug penalty enhancements under 21 U.S.C. § 841(b) extend to other federal statutes with 'results from' language, such as a human-smuggling statute or a healthcare-fraud statute?

sides.position: The § 841(b) no-proximate-cause rule does not extend to other statutes. Sentencing factors for drug crimes are an exception, and that exception should not be applied to a different statute.
cases: United States v. Pineda-Doval, 614 F.3d 1019, 1026–28 (9th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Farley, No. 25-4283 (4th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: The § 841(b) no-proximate-cause rule extends beyond the drug context to other statutes, including a healthcare-fraud statute.
cases: United States v. Webb, 655 F.3d 1238, 1255–56 (11th Cir. 2011)

quote: What is more, our sister circuits are divided about whether (and if so, when) Section 841(b)’s no-proximate-cause rule extends beyond that provision’s specific context.
cite: United States v. Tonya Farley, No. 25-4283 (4th Cir. 2026)
